doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Tristano group and leaving for Kenton
title: Learning Tristano's tunes by ear and the small repertoire
summary: He explains learning lines phrase by phrase, who made harmonies, the tunes' origins on standards, and the band's limited repertoire.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: As far as the more conventional tunes like “Wow”, “Crosscurrent”, “Marionette”, and “Sax of a Kind”, how much rehearsal went into them?
I think we reviewed them each time we played and separately.
How did Lennie teach those to you? Did he write out lead sheets for you?
No. As I have stated in the book Warne and I would pick it up phrase by phrase as he played it and learn the whole tune before writing it down, which is a great way to learn a tune.
How did you work out the harmonies?
They were either suggested by Lennie or Warne added harmony. I didn’t usually do that.
You were playing the lead lines.
Yes…but I think Lennie usually gave the harmony parts.
The Billy Bauer tune “Marionette”; did he teach that to you the same way?
No, I think that was written out.
That’s all unison. It’s a different sound that the other tunes.
On the one tune . . .”Fine and Dandy” Warne wrote the first thirty-two bars, and we played, and the last sixteen bars were mine and those were written out.
That was “Sax of a Kind?”
“Sax of a Kind” based on “Fine and Dandy.”
How many of the other tunes you recorded later, like “Two Not One,” were tunes you had worked out at the time but just didn’t get to record? How big was your repertoire at the time?
“Large repertoire” was not the name of our activities. Our activities were making the most out of a small repertoire.
Other than those tunes you recorded how many other tunes were there?

I would guess, I have to guess because I don’t remember specifically, a handful at best. Neither of those guys wrote original tunes to begin with. I remember Lennie brought in a progression and we never played it. We tried it and the rest of it were variations on standard tunes. On one tune, “Crosscurrent,” there was a different bridge.
That’s altered Rhythm Changes basically.

Yeah, but the bridge was pretty altered. [There were] a couple changes on “Wow”, instead of two-five it was a major two. The emphasis was on solos. I had a feeling to write these things as I do everyday here pretty much. I just got a record of a school in North Carolina. They asked me to do something with the big band. I would send them some of my tunes and the students would make arrangements. It was really nice. I just got a copy.
Really. How did they turn out?
Okay I think.
Do you know the Claire Fisher big band chart on “Lennie’s Pennies”?
I’ve heard that, yeah.
That’s a really good big band chart that Warne and Gary Foster played on. This band worked somewhat doing live gigs for a few years?
